---
title: "Wiring Endpoints, Coordinates, and Network Views"
---

::: {.callout-warning}
## Accepted View semantics; CONVERGING parameter binding

The View and reduction meanings on this page remain accepted Full V1
semantics. The structured authoring examples that supply the Plan are a
separate `CONVERGING` target. Independent parameter definitions, spaces, and
per-point realization are also `CONVERGING`; exact target behavior belongs to
the Parameter System Contract. Exact transforms, capabilities, and failures
belong to the linked Runtime Contract.
:::

## One circuit can support several questions

Consider a floating circuit with physical terminals `floating_plus` and
`floating_minus`. Those two terminals remain part of the authored circuit.
One analysis may inspect both original terminals; another may ask for common
and differential coordinates; a third may retain only the differential
coordinate.

Those are different questions about one Plan. They are not three rewired
circuits.

## Do not collapse three kinds of identity

| Kind | What it means | What it does not mean |
|---|---|---|
| `BusRef` | one declared net used directly for ordinary wiring | a screen position or signal-flow direction |
| `TapRef` | one named contact on its bus, sharing that bus's electrical node | a new node or a layout command |
| `PinRef` | a native terminal or a child boundary exposed to its parent | an analysis coordinate merely because its ID says `tap` |
| `GroundRef` | the scope-local endpoint for the one canonical reference | a public child pin or a page-wide drawing rail |
| node coordinate | the named electrical coordinate exposed for analysis | a drawing location |
| `NetworkViewRef` | an immutable ordered analysis lineage derived from the sealed Plan | a replacement `CircuitPlan` |

A bus can have several taps while retaining one electrical node. A child pin
can expose that node across an ownership boundary. A coordinate can make the
node eligible for analysis. Each role is explicit; none is inferred from the
screen position or from a name such as “readout.”

The target `link(endpoints=(...))` joins two or more eligible `BusRef`,
`TapRef`, or `PinRef` handles as one direct zero-wire relation. It neither
creates an analysis coordinate nor accepts a `GroundRef`. External grounding
instead uses `ground_pins(pins=(...))` on public pins, while intrinsic grounded
branches continue to terminate at `scope.ground`. These declarations may make
several owner-local handles electrically equal without making private child
handles public.

## Original network first, selected View only when needed {#network-view-lineage}

`CircuitRun(plan=...)` seals the complete Plan and supplies `run.original`.
That root `NetworkViewRef` asks about the original network without a
reduction. A later pipeline can derive another immutable Ref:

1. PTC changes the effective topology seen by a selected analysis while
   preserving the declared Port evidence it compensates.
2. `transform_pair()` changes the coordinate representation, such as
   physical plus/minus terminals to common/differential coordinates.
3. `retain()` selects the boundary kept for a particular calculation.

The order matters and remains visible in the Ref lineage. Direct and HB must
either realize that same final View faithfully or fail closed.

Engineer [Chapter 3](../../examples/engineer/chapter-03/01-build.qmd) first
keeps a two-Port feedline/readout request on `run.original`. Engineer
[Chapter 4](../../examples/engineer/chapter-04/03-ptc-core.qmd) then preserves
one four-Port physical Plan while deriving a probe-compensated, retained
feedline View; its optional continuation transforms the same retained lineage.
These are applications of the existing View contract, not reduced replacement
Plans.

Engineer [Chapter 7](../../examples/engineer/chapter-07/01-rlgc.qmd) likewise
keeps one ordered N=2 authoring body distinct from its eight-section finite-pi
compiled model. Its four signal Ports belong to the declared network; the RLGC
reference conductor remains model metadata rather than another Port.

## Values are bound before a View is realized

A `ParameterSet` selects values only for refs already consumed by the Plan. A
`ParameterSpace` asks SCNSim to realize the same Plan and selected View at an
ordered collection of points. Every point reassembles parameter-dependent
native values, transforms, matrices, and reductions; the Plan topology and the
View lineage do not become mutable batch state.

Frequency grids, matrix indices, HB cases, and modes remain Result dimensions,
not parameter axes. A scalar sweep at a fixed transmission-line RLGC value may
track an accepted root branch. This target does not track that same root across
changing complete RLGC matrices; an unsupported request fails rather than
substituting independent root selection.

## The diagram remains a Plan projection

Automatic Semantic Circuit Diagram Layout System (ASCDLS) diagrams explain the
authored Plan or its deterministic compiler expansion. A parameterized diagram
may project one explicit `ParameterSet`, but it does not render a selected
`NetworkViewRef`, PTC-effective topology, solver state, sweep, or Result.
Rendering cannot create or mutate a View.

For the floating example, the original diagram therefore continues to show
`floating_plus` and `floating_minus`. A Result may be indexed by
`floating.common` and `floating.differential`, but those analysis
coordinates are not new physical terminals and are not visually reparented
into the circuit.

## Why this separation matters

Keeping the Plan and View distinct lets one model support several honest
questions while preserving their ancestry. It prevents a compensated probe
from being mistaken for a fabrication change, a transformed coordinate from
being mistaken for a wire, and a retained matrix boundary from being mistaken
for a complete new circuit.

This concept does not introduce a reduced `CircuitPlan`, public access to
anonymous child coordinates, arbitrary transform weights, or backend-specific
port lists.
